---
title: "Coherence constraints on pairwise decisions"
subtitle: "2.6 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Example 1"
description: "Compatibility of isolated-pair decisions with an ordered grade report."
---

Decisions that minimise loss separately for each pair need not correspond to a coherent grade report. Three
independent normal posteriors for A, B and C provide an example. Varying B's mean changes the pairwise direction
probabilities and their loss-minimising actions at withholding cost $\tau$. The density panel describes the posterior
specification. The remaining panels compare the unconstrained pairwise minimum with the minimum over ordered grade
reports. Their difference is the additional expected cost imposed by coherence, which requires all pair decisions
to be represented by a single ordered partition.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Middle at 1.00.** A–B and B–C are withheld separately, while A above C has probability .921 and is stated.
  Transitivity of shared grades contradicts that direction. The minimum coherent risk is .1728. Both optimal reports beneath the curves resolve the conflict by stating an additional direction.
- **Middle at .50.** B moves closer to C. The choices now form {A} > {B, C}, with risk .1410. The coherent
  report reaches the pairwise cost: no extra cost is needed to make the local decisions coherent.
- **Middle at .80.** The mean is just outside the shaded band and the report reaches risk .1589. Additional displayed digits resolve probabilities near the decision boundary.
- **Middle at 1.00, τ .10.** The withholding cost decreases. The best report is {A, B, C}, risk .1000; it withholds the
  confident outer pair too. The pairwise choices remain incompatible with a grade report, but the minimum-risk coherent resolution has changed.
- **Middle at 1.00, τ .25.** The threshold falls to .75, below .760. Every pair is stated, the shaded band vanishes,
  and {A} > {B} > {C} represents the pairwise choices. The density panel is unchanged because τ affects the loss rather than the posterior.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Shared grades assert no equality of true values. They withhold directions, and sharing a grade is transitive.
Kline, Rose and Walters call this a form of a “Condorcet cycle in indifferences”: the conflict is in the shared
grades. These are posteriors set by hand for teaching. The browser evaluates every report of the stated family,
lists equal-risk optima and gives their tolerance; the band is an aid to reading the picture, while compatibility is checked directly against the reports.
:::

Standalone: [coherence](../../embed/coherence.html), for example `?omega2=.81&tau=.20`.

Related applications: [The decision for an isolated pair](one-pair.qmd), [Coherence in a finite three-unit example](coherence-finite.qmd).
